key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst combined with microalgae as a sacrificial agent can substantially boost solar-driven CO2 conversion to CO and CH4 while providing a carbon-negative capture-and-convert pathway.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a scalable catalyst-and-feed strategy for improving photocatalytic CO2 utilization by integrating materials design with biologically derived carbon scavenging.
method: Design an AB2O6-type high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Use Cs/Ba to increase CO2 adsorption, Bi to promote polarization and charge separation, and Nb/Ta to support charge transport.
Compare photocatalytic CO2 reduction under three conditions: no sacrificial agent, microplastics, and microalgae.
evidence_signal: Compared with HEO alone, adding microalgae increased CO production by 10× and CH4 production by 4× in the abstracted evaluation.
watch_item: Microalgae-based operation may require careful control of biomass handling, reaction stability, and separation of products from complex biological feedstocks.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
